item.title: Claude Daily Digest — Friday, Sep 11
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.269 lands with plugin eval suite + WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS 1–256; Managed Agents auto permission mode; /review for PRs tip.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest

Friday, Sep 11, 2026

🆕 What's New

Claude Code v2.1.269 dropped with two headline features:

  • Plugin eval suite — built-in harness for testing and benchmarking Claude Code plugins ⭐
  • WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS (1–256) — tune parallelism for multi-agent workflows; default stays 10 ⭐
  • Bash diff output improvements, OTel vcs.* tagging for observability, and a prompt cache correctness fix

📄 Docs Changes

Managed Agents: auto permission mode — The server now evaluates each agent/MCP tool call and decides to run, deny, or pause for approval. The agent.tool_use and agent.mcp_tool_use events include an evaluation field with the result. Read the docs →

ant beta:sessions connect — Attach your terminal to a live Managed Agents session to follow progress, send messages, and approve/deny tool calls. Add --web to serve the session viewer locally. Read the docs →

💡 Tip of the Day

#13 — Inline /review for PRs

Run /review on an open PR and Claude reads your diff, flags bugs and simplification opportunities, and can post inline GitHub comments — no separate code review tool required. It integrates cleanly into a Claude Code session where you're already making changes.

👀 Have You Seen?

Constitutional AI — Anthropic's core training technique, published as open research, lets Claude self-critique against a set of principles rather than relying purely on human feedback. Why it matters for practitioners: the principles Claude weighs internally mirror the kind of explicit guidance you provide in system prompts. Better-aligned instructions → more predictable, consistent outputs.

Read the research →

item.title: Claude Daily Digest — Tuesday, Sep 8
item.description: No new release (v2.1.263 holds); Fable 5.1 lands on Bedrock; custom slash commands tip; vision support spotlight.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest
Tuesday, Sep 8

What's New

No new Claude Code release today. Latest is v2.1.263 (September 6). Stable day on the release front.

Claude Fable 5.1 on Amazon Bedrock — now generally available. Worth evaluating for complex reasoning tasks where Sonnet hits its ceiling. Existing IAM and VPC configurations apply — no new integration work needed.

Tip of the Day — #10: Custom slash commands

Create .claude/commands/your-command.md in your repo and it becomes a /your-command you can call in any Claude Code session.

The file's content becomes the prompt. Check it in with the repo and every engineer on the team gets the same command — no manual setup, no drift.

Have You Seen? — Vision support

Claude Code reads images. Paste a screenshot into the prompt, drag in a file, or reference a path — Claude analyzes it directly.

Pair with claude --print and a screenshot tool in CI for automated visual regression checks.

item.title: Claude Daily Digest — Monday, Sep 7
item.description: Labor Day edition: Claude Code v2.1.264; OTel spans for tool use; MCP sampling tip; plus a look at Prompt Caching.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest
Monday, Sep 7

What's New

Claude Code v2.1.264 — adds OpenTelemetry spans for tool use events. Now you can trace individual tool calls (Bash, Read, Write, etc.) as separate spans in your OTel backend. Useful for performance profiling and debugging slow agents.

MCP: Sampling support — MCP servers can now request LLM completions from the host client. This enables servers to perform AI-powered operations without requiring their own API key — the client handles the inference.

Tip of the Day — #11: MCP sampling for server-side AI

If you're building an MCP server, you can now have it request completions from the connected Claude client using the sampling API. Great for AI-powered tools that need LLM inference without managing their own API keys.

Have You Seen? — Prompt Caching

Prompt caching lets Claude reuse prefilled context across multiple requests at 90% cost reduction. Particularly powerful for agents that repeatedly query the same codebase or documentation. The cache is transparent — just structure your prompts so stable content comes first.

item.title: Claude Daily Digest — Sunday, Sep 6
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.263: OpenTelemetry hooks, CLAUDE.md auto-include globs, and MCP reconnect improvements. Tip: use OTel for agent debugging.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest
Sunday, Sep 6

What's New

Claude Code v2.1.263 — ships OpenTelemetry hooks, CLAUDE.md glob support for auto-includes, and improved MCP server reconnection behavior.

The OTel hooks let you pipe agent telemetry into your existing observability stack (Datadog, Honeycomb, Grafana, etc.) without extra instrumentation.

Tip of the Day — #9: CLAUDE.md glob patterns

In CLAUDE.md, you can use @path/to/**/*.md glob patterns to automatically include matching files as context. Useful for keeping Claude informed about all docs in a particular folder without listing each file manually.

Have You Seen? — Constitutional AI

Anthropic's Constitutional AI research trains models to self-critique against a set of principles — this is the foundation of Claude's harmlessness training. For practitioners: the principles Claude weighs internally mirror the kind of explicit guidance you put in system prompts. Well-aligned instructions get more consistent outputs as a direct result.

item.title: Claude Daily Digest — Saturday, Sep 5
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.261: workflow concurrency cap, hooks for tool events, glob auto-includes for CLAUDE.md. Plus a look at extended thinking.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest
Saturday, Sep 5

What's New

Claude Code v2.1.261 — three notable additions: workflow concurrency cap (avoid runaway parallelism), hooks for tool events (pre/post Bash, Read, Write), and CLAUDE.md glob auto-includes.

Tip of the Day — #8: Hooks for tool events

Wire shell commands to pre/post tool events in your Claude Code config. Example: log every Bash invocation to a file, run a linter after every Write, or ping a webhook after a commit. Hooks run in your shell, so they have full system access.

Have You Seen? — Extended Thinking

Extended thinking lets Claude "think" before responding — the model produces a chain-of-thought scratchpad that isn't shown in the final answer. For hard problems (logic, multi-step math, ambiguous requirements), enabling extended thinking gives significantly more reliable outputs than standard mode. Available via the API with a thinking block in the response.

item.title: Claude Daily Digest — September 4, 2026
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.259 + v2.1.258: Workbench improvements, MCP resource subscriptions. Plus: TodoWrite for task tracking.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest
September 4, 2026

What's New

Claude Code v2.1.259 + v2.1.258 — workbench improvements (better output formatting for large tool responses), plus MCP resource subscriptions — servers can now push resource updates to the client.

Tip of the Day — #7: TodoWrite for task tracking

Use the TodoWrite / TodoRead tools to have Claude maintain a live task list during long sessions. Especially useful when you're working on multi-step refactors — Claude can track what's done and what's next without you needing to re-explain the state.

Have You Seen? — MCP Resource Subscriptions

MCP servers can now push updates to connected clients. If you're building a server that monitors a file, database, or live data stream, subscriptions let it notify Claude automatically instead of polling. Check the MCP 1.2 spec for the subscription protocol details.

item.title: Claude Daily Digest — Thu, Sep 3
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.256 + v2.1.257: codebase-wide search, improved file tree. Plus: /compact for context management; Artifacts for generated content.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest
Thu, Sep 3

What's New

Claude Code v2.1.256 + v2.1.257 — codebase-wide search improvements (smarter file ranking, better context window usage) and an improved file tree view for large monorepos.

Tip of the Day — #6: /compact for context management

When a long session eats your context window, run /compact to summarize and compress the conversation while keeping the key decisions and code in play. Combine with a CLAUDE.md that lists your session goals so Claude re-orients quickly after compaction.

Have You Seen? — Artifacts

Claude.ai's Artifacts feature renders generated content — HTML, React components, SVGs, Markdown — in a live preview panel alongside the conversation. For Claude Code users: useful for prototyping UI components before committing them to your project.

item.title: Claude Daily Digest — Tuesday, Sep 2, 2026
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.254: parallel sub-agents, Managed Agents SDK GA. Plus: multi-agent workflows explained; a look at Claude.ai Projects.
item.content:encoded:
Claude Daily Digest
Tuesday, Sep 2, 2026

What's New

Claude Code v2.1.254 — introduces parallel sub-agents (spawn background agents from within a session) and ships the Managed Agents SDK as GA.

Tip of the Day — #5: Multi-agent workflows

Use the Agent tool to spawn sub-agents for parallelizable work — code review while tests run, multiple search angles at once. Each sub-agent gets a clean context; the orchestrator synthesizes results. Key: the sub-agent's final response is its return value, so tell it to return structured data, not human-facing prose.

Have You Seen? — Claude.ai Projects

Projects give Claude persistent context across sessions — upload your docs, codebase snippets, or style guides once, and Claude retains them without you re-pasting each time. For practitioners: pair Projects with a custom system prompt tuned to your domain for a lightweight, no-infra knowledge base.

Have You Seen? Addendum — System Prompts — Now Public — Anthropic published their internal system prompts in August 2026.
